title: The Deep-Sea Beacon
summary: Dive to a shipwreck: tilt, flip and size wire hoops over a seabed magnet so the changing flux lights a sealed beacon just right.
subject: physics
concepts: Induced emf in a loop in a solenoid
Average emf of a turning coil
No change of flux, no emf
learningOutcome: The student can find the flux BA cos θ and its change, and use ε = N ΔΦ/Δt for a dying field, a solenoid’s rising current, a 180° flip and the slope of a flux graph.

levels.title: Pad switch-off
levels.adds: Baseline: Φ = BA cos θ through a tilted hoop; when the field dies, ε = NΔΦ/Δt lights the bulb only while the flux changes (Section 6.3, Example 6.2).
hints: θ is the angle between the field and the normal to the hoop: flat is 0°, edge-on is 90°.
The flux linkage NBA cos θ falls to zero, so ε = NBA cos θ / Δt.
Solve for cos θ, then find the angle. A bigger tilt means less flux.

levels.title: The charging sleeve
levels.adds: New idea: inside a long solenoid B = μ₀nI, so a rising current changes the flux and ε = Nμ₀nA ΔI/Δt (Ex 6.3).
hints: Turn n into turns per metre: 20 per cm is 2000 per m.
The flux through one turn of the ring is μ₀nI × πr².
ε = N μ₀ n πr² ΔI/Δt; solve for r.

levels.title: The flip
levels.adds: More steps: a 180° flip takes the flux from +BA to −BA, so ε = 2NBA/t and the current is ε/R (Example 6.3).
hints: A = πr² with r in metres.
The change of flux linkage is 2NBA, not zero.
I = ε/R = 2NBA/(tR); solve for the flip time t.

levels.title: The flux program
levels.adds: Apply it: the emf is the slope of the flux graph, so the steepest step, rising or falling, flashes brightest (Section 6.4).
hints: Read the flux at each second from the grid; each step lasts 1 s.
1 mWb per second is 1 mV per turn. Take the size of the slope.
The steepest step must give exactly the rating: N = rating ÷ steepest emf per turn.

misconceptions: The emf depends on the flux itself, not on how fast it changes
A steady flux through a coil induces a steady emf
Turning a coil through 180° gives no change in flux
Only a rising flux gives a big emf; a falling one does not count
Flux is greatest when the coil’s plane is along the field
